newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil cargoes chase U.S. arb, barges slumber.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil cargoes chase U.S. arb, barges slumber.

text.p: Flat demand and drooping premiums in NWE drove most gas oil activity out of the region on Friday, chasing widening arbitrage opportunities in the United States and Asia, traders said.
About 120,000 tonnes of Russian was due in the United States in the next week under NWE arbitrage in addition to a previously reported 60,000 tonne vessel also headed to the U.S., they said.

The two 60,000 tonne cargoes were done at levels equivalent to around $227 a tonne. Russian gas oil for prompt delivery was around $1.75/2.75 over Jan IPE futures contract, which ended down $2.75 at $215.
While arbitrage efforts concentrated mostly on 60,000 tonne cargoes efforts are also being made to fix smaller vessels.
Refinery grade heating oil cargoes stagnated at Jan IPE +$4/5 in weak trade. Low sulphur diesel was around Jan IPE +$13/15.
"It's all pretty dead," a trader said.
Barges saw modest activity. Heating oil was slightly firmer at $215 to 217.75 a tonne outright for delivery from prompt to January 5, equivalent to Jan IPE -$1/+$1.
Low sulphur was quiet, at around Jan IPE +$13/15.
